copy.headline: ROOM ABOVE TWO HUNDRED
copy.deck: The week the pressure reached everyone
copy.body: By Sunday night, the Commonwealth had learned that a number could become a weapon without anyone lifting a blade. Two teams had crossed two hundred. One sent a hamburger to a birthday party; another brought an army to a mountain gate. A centaur was chasing an outlaw through Highland mud. In the eastern ruins, a river quietly made a mockery of Red Leopards’ sandbags, while a second gust carried the same storm's reach to a court farther inland. Seven Deadly Chins found the one household that needed quiet and arrived with a jackhammer. Slob on my Dobb made a beer delivery through a swamp whose owner could no longer command the road. The front belonged to El Niño; the humiliations belonged to the men who chose them. With four regular-season games now remaining, the question was no longer simply who won. It was what each result would leave behind.

copy.headline: KEEP THE WHOLE LEAGUE IN VIEW
copy.deck: Commissioner’s note • After Week 10
copy.body: There is a difference between being beaten and having to live with the evidence. A score is entered once. A birthday photograph is shown forever. A broken hoop stays broken until someone fixes it. The owner of a swamp still has to watch the next truck drive through. That is the Commonwealth we have spent seasons building, and it is why this league is more than six boxes on a scoreboard. But our stories do not outrank the standings. Nobody is going to Cancún by mathematical decree until the last route is closed. Nobody is healed because a reserve slot looks full. The numbers have settled, and six teams now share 6–4 records. The next week will ask each of us what we have left to field.

copy.headline: Everybody Gets a View
copy.deck: The Chili Cheesers vs D0nkey K0ng
copy.body: The Chili Cheesers has always understood the value of a crowd. At last week's cookout he chose the victim, the serving and the moment everyone laughed. Now he circles the Arsenal's Highland ring with the crowd above him, searching for an exit while the four-legged centaur closes behind, lasso turning overhead. Every open gate seems to belong to D0nkey K0ng. The same storm that wet the rails has made the ground a poor place to sprint in expensive boots.

copy.headline: One More Bag
copy.deck: Red Leopards vs El Niño
copy.body: The river did not arrive as a wall. It climbed a little, found a gap, and waited for Red Leopards to believe the last sandbag had solved it. The old goal leaned over a pitch still carrying last week's damage. Red Leopards shifted another bag into place. The water went around it. In 2022, he had beaten El Niño twice and carried thirteen wins into the semifinal. It was not the strength of the old season he remembered now, but how little of it had mattered on the night it ended.

copy.headline: THE ROADS BETWEEN
copy.deck: The same front, different ground
copy.body: On the exposed coast, water finds the old damage. Farther inland, gusts take the trees and banners. In the southern wetlands, runoff arrives later through familiar channels. Up here, travelers tighten their covers and the lamps come on early. The Commonwealth has not changed places. The weather has reached more of them.

Last year Dr. Duckhook came within four tenths of stopping this rival's championship path. Tonight he opens the door to him.
